title: Checkpoint fetch postmortem (scratch)
body:
Summary:
This is my working scratch for the SEV on model load failures when fetching weights for 'redwood-open-7b-v2' (manifest v3). Symptoms: intermittent "EOFError: unexpected end of data" and later "ValueError: unknown dtype 'q4_0' in header" coming from the safetensors parser in the fetch worker. Failures only surface when serving on prod region-us-west1 and not when I pull the objects locally from my laptop (odd).

Timeline and quick notes:
- 2025-09-08 09:13 UTC: first alerts from canary (error rate spike on /models/load endpoint).
- 2025-09-08 09:14 UTC: spike correlated with a single client rollout that requested model: redwood-open-7b-v2@2025-09-08-08.
- 2025-09-08 09:20 UTC: SRE pointed to repeated 499/transport errors from fetcher logs with transfer id trace:tid=tid-7d3b.
- 2025-09-08 09:33 UTC: replicated failure on staging when we forced the serving runtime to fetch from GCS by deleting local cache.

Key hypothesis threads I'm tracking (ordered by likelihood):
1) Partial object composition / multipart edge case in GCS: composed objects can have different internal CRC/md5 and streaming range semantics. If an object was re-composed during a background process or lifecycle job, range requests can return odd truncations.
2) Transport chunk boundary corruption: our download helper uses 16MB chunking. Observed EOFs at offsets that are multiples of 16,777,216 bytes. Could be bug in the chunk reassembly when a connection reset occurs and we retry with overlapping range.
3) Header/format mismatch: some builds of the safetensors exporter wrote a nonstandard dtype tag (e.g., 'q4_0' vs 'q4_0_fast') and an older safetensors Python library in the fetch worker throws ValueError rather than a graceful fallback.
4) Compression / double-compression: upstream process mistakenly compressed the tarball and also created a .safetensors that contains compressed blobs; our streaming reader expects raw safetensors.
5) Object lifecycle/archival placeholder: a lifecycle rule may have briefly replaced the object with a 0-byte placeholder metadata object while a long compose finished.

Commands and quick smoke checks I ran (raw):
- Check object size + metadata from prod: 
  gsutil ls -L gs://models-prod/redwood-open-7b-v2/2025-09-08/manifest.json  # shows composite:Composite (component count: 4) size: 124,578,432 bytes

- Head and range checks (on prod worker node):
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "https://storage.googleapis.com/models-prod/redwood-open-7b-v2/2025-09-08/weights.safetensors"
  curl -s --range 0-64 https://storage.googleapis.com/models-prod/.../weights.safetensors | xxd -l 80
  curl -s --range 16777216-16777280 https://storage.googleapis.com/models-prod/.../weights.safetensors | xxd -l 80  # repeated EOF observed here in logs

- Local retrieval (works):
  gsutil cp gs://models-prod/redwood-open-7b-v2/2025-09-08/weights.safetensors /tmp/weights.safetensors  # file size matches 124,578,432 bytes
  sha256sum /tmp/weights.safetensors  # abcdef... (matches manifest sha256)

- Remote node retrieval (intermittent fail):
  python -c "import requests; r=requests.get("https://storage.googleapis.com/.../weights.safetensors", stream=True); from itertools import islice; print(len(list(islice(r.iter_content(65536), 0, 400))))"
  # sometimes returns fewer chunks and then r.raise_for_status() triggers EOF decoding error in safetensors loader.

- Low-level header probe using hexdump:
  curl -s --range 0-512 https://storage.googleapis.com/.../weights.safetensors | xxd -g 1 -c 32 | sed -n '1,8p'
  # header looks OK locally, but on failing worker the same range returned fewer bytes.

- Compare md5/crc32c from metadata vs manifest:
  gsutil stat gs://models-prod/.../weights.safetensors  # md5: HHHH, crc32c: QQQQ
  jq '.files["weights.safetensors"].sha256' manifest.json  # sha256 matches but md5 didn't line up on some runs

Repro script I used to stress-range requests (attached as snippet in body below). Run on worker nodes to mimic fetcher chunking and retries. If you run this from the node that fails, you often reproduce the EOF quickly.

--- python repro (very small) ---
import requests, sys
url = sys.argv[1]
CHUNK = 16*1024*1024
pos = 0
buf = b''
while True:
    r = requests.get(url, headers={"Range": f"bytes={pos}-{pos+CHUNK-1}"}, stream=True, timeout=10)
    data = r.content
    if not data:
        print('empty chunk at', pos); break
    buf += data
    pos += len(data)
    print('got', len(data), 'at', pos)
    if len(data) < CHUNK:
        print('short chunk', len(data)); break
print('total', len(buf))
# saves to file for safetensors loader
with open('/tmp/repro.weights', 'wb') as f: f.write(buf)

--- end snippet ---

Errors and logs (copied raw where possible):
- serving-worker[worker-7d3b] ERROR load: EOFError: unexpected end of data while parsing tensor data for 'model.layers.4.attn.q.weight' (offset 16777216)
- fetcher[tid-7d3b] WARN download: retries exhausted for range 16777216-33554431 (connection reset)
- safetensors.loader ERROR: ValueError: Unknown dtype 'q4_0' encountered while parsing metadata (this exception patched in local debug build to log header bytes)
- gcs logs: compose operation started by user:bot@infra on 2025-09-07T23:34:12Z, components: [weights.part-1, weights.part-2, weights.part-3, weights.part-4]

Notes on weird observations:
- Local laptop cp -> always ok. But when I run gsutil cp from the failing worker, it succeeds ~60% of the time and fails the rest. Network flakiness on that node is possible but I haven't seen other objects fail similarly.
- Error offsets cluster at 16MB boundaries -> strongly suggests chunking / range request logic bug.
- Metadata CRCs/matching: manifest sha256 matches the object when fetched locally, but md5 recorded in bucket metadata sometimes mismatches (GCS md5 for composite objects can be different due to compose behavior). We rely on sha256 in manifest, not GCS md5.
- Some older exporter runs produced stray 'meta.bin' entries in the safetensors file which confuse our streaming parser when chunk boundaries split metadata.

Immediate mitigations applied (and results):
- Switched the fetcher to single-request mode for this model (no chunked range requests). Result: load success rate improved to ~98% in the affected cluster, latency up ~+70ms.
- Rolled back the client rollout that triggered a high rate of concurrent cold loads. Result: error rate fell to baseline.
- SRE restarted the failing node pool (suspected noisy networking). Result: partial improvement but not full resolution.

Next investigative actions (TODOs):
- [ ] Add robust validation in fetcher: when a chunk is short, attempt overlapping re-fetch with small backoff and verify header magic bytes before appending.
- [ ] Add explicit crc64/sha256 verification for every composed object after fetch completes and fail early with improved error message (include component list).
- [ ] Add diagnostic endpoint to fetcher to stream the first N bytes with timestamps and transfer-ids (to help correlate GCS compose operations).
- [ ] Re-run a controlled compose test: create a composite object composed of 4 parts, then issue parallel range requests to see if GCS returns atomic consistency across ranges during compose. Document outcome.
- [ ] Validate safetensors exporter used in CI for any dtype variant tags and add a compatibility shim in the loader for known legacy tags.
- [ ] Add a temporary feature flag to force single-request fetch for any model marked as 'composite' in the manifest.

Hypothesis validation plan (explicit):
- To test hypothesis #1 (compose inconsistency): create object A,B,C,D. Compose -> start returning ranges while compose still in progress (simulate by using a placeholder writer), monitor range responses for overlaps/truncation.
- To test hypothesis #2 (chunk reassembly bug): run repro script under heavy packet drop (tc qdisc netem) and simulate retry code paths to ensure overlap ranges and concatenation logic is correct. Unit tests to assert idempotency of overlapping recombines.
- To test hypothesis #3 (dtype mismatch): generate a small safetensors with legacy dtype tag and run loader; make loader fallback to metadata-only parse then map to the current dtype table.

Breadcrumbs to keep if we need to escalate:
- failing trace id: tid-7d3b (logs pinned in pagerduty incident 2025-09-08-9321)
- bucket: gs://models-prod/redwood-open-7b-v2/2025-09-08/weights.safetensors
- compose op logged at: 2025-09-07T23:34:12Z by bot@infra
- local sha256 of good copy: abcdef0123456789deadbeef... (put in secret store if needed)

Notes to self (less formal):
- If this is a GCS compose atomicity quirk, we should avoid range-chunked streaming for composite objects until we have a robust overlap+verify path.
- Add a tiny unit test that forces chunk boundary on metadata region (create a fake safetensors where metadata header ends exactly at 16MB boundary) to ensure loader gracefully handles header split across chunks.
- When retrying overlapping ranges, always request a small leading overlap (e.g., 64 bytes) and check magic bytes to align writes.

Appendix: quick grep-able error snippets for searching logs:
- "unexpected end of data while parsing tensor data"
- "retries exhausted for range"
- "Unknown dtype 'q4_0'"
- "compose operation started by user:bot@infra"

End of scratch. Will keep updating as I run the compose tests and add unit-tests. If anyone picks this up: start with the single-request config toggle and run the repro script from the affected node pool.
